extracted.intended_audience: potential parties, petitioners, counsel, licensees, and members of the public who wish to comment on or seek hearing/party status or access to SUNSI in NRC license amendment proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive requirements for submitting public comments, requesting hearings or petitions to intervene, and requesting/obtaining access to Sensitive Unclassified Non-Safeguards Information (SUNSI) in NRC license amendment proceedings. Covers deadlines, filing formats (E-Filing), standing/need determinations, protective order/NDAs, and the target processing schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments submission (deadline and methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received by March 26, 2026. The NRC encourages electronic comment submission through the Federal rulemaking website (https://www.regulations.gov) and requests inclusion of Docket ID NRC-2026-0463, facility name, unit number(s), docket number(s), application date, and subject in comment submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include identifying or contact information you do not want publicly disclosed; the NRC will post all comment submissions at Regulations.gov and enter them into ADAMS and does not routinely edit submissions to remove identifying information. If aggregating comments, inform contributors not to include identifying/contact information they do not want disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to request a hearing / petition to intervene (deadline & rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after publication, any person whose interest may be affected may file a request for a hearing and petition for leave to intervene. Petitions shall be filed in accordance with the Commission's 'Agency Rules of Practice and Procedure' in 10 CFR part 2 and interested persons should consult 10 CFR 2.309.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be filed no later than 60 days from publication in accordance with the Electronic Submissions (E-Filing) section. Motions for leave to file new or amended contentions filed after the deadline will not be entertained absent a presiding officer finding of good cause satisfying the three factors in 10 CFR 2.309(c)(1)(i)-(iii). States/local governmental bodies/Federally recognized Indian Tribes may petition under 10 CFR 2.309(h) or participate as non-parties under 10 CFR 2.315(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: No Significant Hazards Consideration (NSHC) criteria (10 CFR 50.92)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 10 CFR 50.92, the Commission's proposed determination that an amendment involves no significant hazards consideration (NSHC) means that operation in accordance with the proposed amendments would not: (1) involve a significant increase in the probability or consequences of an accident previously evaluated, (2) create the possibility of a new or different kind of accident from any accident previously evaluated, or (3) involve a significant reduction in a margin of safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission bases proposed NSHC determinations on the licensee's application and provides the basis for each amendment's proposed determination in the notice. The Commission may issue amendments before the normal 60-day wait if it makes a final NSHC determination or if circumstances (e.g., avoiding derating/shutdown) make prompt action necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request access to SUNSI (definition of potential party)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'potential party' is any person who intends to participate as a party by demonstrating standing and filing an admissible contention under 10 CFR 2.309.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only potential parties (as defined) who believe access to SUNSI is necessary to respond to the notice may request SUNSI access under these procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for initial SUNSI access requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days after publication of the notice of hearing or opportunity for hearing, any potential party who believes access to SUNSI is necessary to respond must request access. Requests submitted later than 10 days will not be considered absent a showing of good cause explaining why the request could not have been filed earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial SUNSI access request should be submitted as described in paragraph C (see footnote): as a letter to the Office of the Secretary with a copy to the Deputy General Counsel, not via the NRC E-Filing system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and routing of SUNSI access requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The requestor shall submit a letter requesting permission to access SUNSI to the Office of the Secretary, U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, with a copy to the Deputy General Counsel for Licensing, Hearings, and Enforcement. Email addresses and expedited delivery/courier addresses are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact address/email instructions in the order. The footnote clarifies that while hearing/petition filings must comply with E-Filing, the initial SUNSI request should be submitted as described (i.e., to the offices specified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of a SUNSI access request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include: (1) a description of the licensing action with a citation to the Federal Register notice; (2) the name and address of the potential party and a description of the potential party's particularized interest that could be harmed by the action; and (3) the identity of the individual or entity requesting access and the requestor's basis for the need for the information to meaningfully participate, explaining why publicly available versions would be insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must explain why publicly available versions would not provide the basis and specificity for a proffered contention.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC staff determination criteria and timing for SUNSI requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days of receipt of the request the NRC staff will determine whether: (1) there is a reasonable basis to believe the requestor is likely to establish standing to participate; and (2) the requestor has established a legitimate need for access to SUNSI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If staff finds both elements, it will notify the requestor in writing and begin document processing (redactions/review). If staff finds no need or no likelihood of standing, the requestor may file a motion seeking reversal within specified deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and paperwork for access if granted (Protective Order/NDA/Affidavit)
rubrics_metrics.description: If access is granted the written notification will contain instructions on how to obtain copies and any conditions that may apply. Conditions may include signing a draft Non-Disclosure Agreement or Affidavit, or a Protective Order setting forth terms to prevent unauthorized or inadvertent disclosure of SUNSI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRC staff will file a motion for a Protective Order and proposed NDA/Affidavit (or applicant/licensee will file a proposed NDA/Affidavit). Executed NDAs/Affidavits must be filed by the deadline set in the protective order schedule (attachment schedule shows A+3 as deadline to file executed agreements). Access is provided consistent with the Protective Order decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for filing contentions based on SUNSI
rubrics_metrics.description: Any contentions based upon information received as a result of the request for SUNSI must be filed by the requestor no later than 25 days after receipt of (or access to) that information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if more than 25 days remain between the requestor's receipt/access to the information and the deadline for filing all other contentions (as established in the notice), the requestor may file its SUNSI contentions by that later deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of denials of SUNSI access (challenge process and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the NRC staff denies access after making determinations on standing and need, the staff shall immediately notify the requestor in writing, briefly stating reasons. The requestor may challenge the adverse determination by filing a challenge within five days of receipt with the presiding officer (or designated judge). Further appeals are made pursuant to 10 CFR 2.311.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The staff must file a copy of its access determination with the presiding officer (or Chief Administrative Judge) as appropriate. The E-Filing requirements apply to appeals of NRC staff determinations because they must be served on a presiding officer or Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of grants of SUNSI access (third-party challenges)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party other than the requestor may challenge an NRC staff determination granting access to SUNSI whose release would harm that party's interest independent of the proceeding. Such a challenge must be filed within 5 days of notification and with the presiding officer (or designated judge). Further appeals under 10 CFR 2.311.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If challenges are filed, normal litigation processes for disputes concerning access apply and interlocutory review availability by the Commission is governed by 10 CFR 2.311.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 1 — Target schedule for processing SUNSI access requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The order provides a day-by-day target schedule: Day 0 = publication; Day 10 = deadline for SUNSI access requests; Day 20 = NRC staff informs requestor of determinations; Day 25 = deadline to file motions to reverse NRC staff finding of no need/standing or deadline for parties to file motions to reverse grant; Day 30 = NRC staff reply to motions; Day 40 (Receipt +30) = deadline for NRC staff to complete processing and file motion for Protective Order and proposed NDA/Affidavit; A = issuance of presiding officer decision on Protective Order; A+3 = deadline for filing executed NDAs/Affidavits and access provided; A+28 = deadline for submission of contentions developed using SUNSI (with earlier-later caveat); A+53 = answers to contentions; A+60 = petitioner/intervenor reply; >A+60 = decision on contention admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This schedule is the general target and the order expects timely consideration of requests and motions to minimize unnecessary delays in adjudicatory proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Submissions (E-Filing) requirements for adjudicatory proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents filed in NRC adjudicatory proceedings must be filed in accordance with 10 CFR 2.302. The E-Filing process requires participants to submit and serve adjudicatory documents over the internet (or mail on electronic storage media if an exemption is granted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least 10 days prior to the filing deadline a participant should contact the Office of the Secretary to request a digital ID certificate and advise the Secretary that the participant will be submitting a petition or other adjudicatory document. After a digital ID is obtained and a docket is created, documents must be submitted in Portable Document Format (PDF). A filing is complete when submitted through the E-Filing system and must be submitted no later than 11:59 p.m. ET on the due date. The system time-stamps submissions and emails confirmations and distributes access to OGC and others who have advised the Secretary they wish to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-Filing exemptions and alternative filing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants who believe they have good cause for not submitting documents electronically must file an exemption request in accordance with 10 CFR 2.302(g) with their initial paper filing stating why there is good cause and requesting authorization to continue paper submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such filings must comply with 10 CFR 2.302(b)-(d). Participants granted an exemption under 2.302(g)(2) must still meet the electronic formatting requirement in 2.302(g)(1), unless also granted an exemption from that formatting requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting, privacy, and copyrighted material guidance for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants are requested not to include personal privacy information (e.g., SSNs, home addresses, personal phone numbers) in filings unless required by NRC regulation or law. With respect to copyrighted works, except for limited excerpts that serve the purpose of adjudicatory filings and would constitute fair use, participants should not include copyrighted materials in their submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and participants must consider public posting on Regulations.gov and ADAMS when deciding what information to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to obtain publicly available documents (ADAMS and PDR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly available information related to this action may be obtained via Regulations.gov (Docket ID NRC-2026-0463), NRC's ADAMS Public Documents collection (https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/adams.html) by using the ADAMS accession numbers provided, or by appointment at the NRC's Public Document Room (PDR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ADAMS problems contact the PDR reference staff; the ADAMS accession number for each referenced document is provided the first time it is mentioned in the document. To visit the PDR, make an appointment via email or phone during business hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-Filing practical assistance and help desk availability
rubrics_metrics.description: A person filing electronically may seek assistance from the NRC's Electronic Filing Help Desk via the 'Contact Us' link on NRC's e-submissions page, by email (MSHD.Resource@nrc.gov), or by toll-free phone at 1-866-672-7640.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Help Desk is available between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m., ET, Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial access request submission method (footnote clarification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnote: While a request for hearing or petition to intervene must comply with the E-Filing Rule, the initial request to access SUNSI under these procedures should be submitted as described in paragraph C (i.e., to the Office of the Secretary and copy to the Deputy General Counsel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the E-Filing system for the initial SUNSI access request; follow the specified letter/email addresses set out in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of NSHC final determination on timing of hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission makes a final NSHC determination for any license amendment, any hearing on those amendments will take place after issuance; if the final determination is that the amendment involves a significant hazards consideration, any hearing would take place before issuance unless imminent danger requires immediate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission normally will not issue amendments until 60 days after publication; it may issue them earlier if a final NSHC determination is made or other exigent circumstances exist (e.g., to avoid derating/shutdown).
